title: Conditions of Enrolment in a Mountain Dining Plans Plan
content:
A plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range is opened for a named holder who meets the plan's minimum age, and the plan's enrolment fee is raised with it. The plan comes into use only once a load of at least the plan's first load amount has cleared.

## The two conditions, set out as condition and result

**Condition of opening.** The person the plan is registered to must meet the minimum holder age the plan carries. The plan is opened in the name of that holder, for the season it is sold for, on the household account it belongs to, and the plan's enrolment fee is raised against the account at the same time.

**Condition of coming into use.** A plan that has been opened stands in the enrolled state. It moves to the active state, in which the card may be used at the collective's outlets, when a load has cleared and that load is at least the plan's first load amount. Nothing short of that brings it into use: the plan comes into use only on that condition being met.

## The two states, and what each means

| State of the plan | What the record shows | What the card does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| enrolled | the plan has been opened for the named holder and the enrolment fee has been raised | not yet spendable |
| active | a load of at least the plan's first load amount has cleared | spendable at the collective's outlets |

## Worked readings on hypothetical figures

Take a plan whose first load amount is $500.00. A load of $500.00 clears: the amount is at least the plan's first load amount, so the condition is met and the plan comes into use. A load of $499.00 clears instead: the amount falls short of the plan's first load amount, the condition on which the plan comes into use is not met, and the plan stands in the enrolled state still.

The enrolment fee attaches to the opening of the plan, not to the plan coming into use, so it is raised on the plan that has been opened whether or not a load has yet cleared.
